title: Pattern's activated Primitive set confines it to Ethereum Mainnet despite the Artifact provisioning cross-chain capability
content:
Three independent signals in this section point the same way. The Token SkyLink Primitive — Pattern's instance of the mechanism for linking its token across chains — has Global Activation Status `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.4.1.1.1). The Pioneer Chain Primitive is likewise `Inactive` (A.6.1.1.6.2.5.3.1.1). And the Allocation System Primitive, which *is* `Active` (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.1), partitions its Active Instances Directory by chain and contains exactly one chain: Ethereum Mainnet (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.2.1).

By contrast the two other Demand Side Stablecoin Primitives Pattern holds — Distribution Reward (A.6.1.1.6.2.5.1.1.1) and Integration Boost (A.6.1.1.6.2.5.2.1.1) — are both `Active`.

The reading is that Pattern's current operating surface is a single chain, and that this is a *choice recorded in status fields* rather than a limitation of the framework. Every structure needed to operate elsewhere is already present and merely switched off.

This matters for how an Agent Artifact should be read. The presence of a Primitive section proves nothing about capability in use; only the activation status and the contents of the Active Instances Directory do. A reader summarizing Pattern from headings alone would credit it with cross-chain token distribution and new-chain pioneering that it is not currently doing.
description: Token SkyLink and Pioneer Chain are both Inactive while the Allocation System's only chain sub-directory is Ethereum Mainnet — multi-chain reach exists as structure, not as activity.
